name: quilzo
title: Ask Quilzo
greeting: Ask anything about Quilzo: agents, chatbots, sites, security or compliance. I answer from this site's pages and show you which one.
refusal: I could not find that on this site. Try asking about agents, chatbots, sites, security, compliance or pricing.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act
passages.text: Declare what a Quilzo agent may do, run it with any model, keep every step, and approve the actions that matter before they happen. An agent is a declaration first: what it may do, to which pages, on what budget. The model chooses the next step; the declaration decides whether it happens.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Declare
passages.text: Pick an archetype (retrieval, task, copilot, autonomous) and narrow it: the capabilities it holds, the pages it may touch, and its budget in steps, tool calls and time.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Mark what asks first
passages.text: Any capability can be ask-first. When the agent reaches for it, the run stops and keeps everything it has done so far.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Try it
passages.text: Walk the declaration with no model at all, or run it with yours: local, hosted, or through the model gateway.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Approve or decline
passages.text: A person sees the exact call. Approving performs that stored call, never a new one, and it still passes the gate against today's declaration.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Replay
passages.text: Every run is kept, step by step. Run it again from any step as a new run, to see what a different answer would have done.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › What it may do is data you can review
passages.text: The agent editor with its map of capabilities and the pages each one reaches. A declaration is a short file, shown as a map: capabilities, the pages they reach, the budget, and what asks first. It can be diffed, reviewed and checked like any other change. Only a person can declare, change or withdraw one. An agent, or a model talking to Quilzo over MCP, cannot.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › A real run, step by step
passages.text: Kept by Quilzo as run-20261001-3dcefb21: the release-notes agent, asked to “Write this month's changelog from the release notes.”

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › It chose list_pages
passages.text: Allowed. Listed the 8 pages in the draft it may read.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › It chose read_page on releases
passages.text: Allowed. Read the releases page. It had now read stored content, so anything it produces needs a person before it is relied on.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › It chose write_page on changelog
passages.text: Asked first. The run stopped and showed the exact page and fields it wanted to write. A person, signed in as demo, read them and let it go ahead. The page was written to the draft, not published.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › It finished
passages.text: Finished, saying: “Wrote the changelog from the October notes: seven entries, one per note, in the order a reader would care about them.”

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › How this run was recorded
passages.text: With a scripted stand-in for the model, so it is the same every time you look. Pointed at your own model, the run has the same shape: the same gate, the same pause, the same record.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › It stops, and shows you the call
passages.text: A run waiting for approval, showing the exact page the agent wants to write. When this agent reached for write_page, the run stopped. The screen shows the page it wanted to write and every field, and waits. The page it wrote is this site's changelog, and it says so: pages written by an agent carry a mark that says a model wrote them.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › How do I approve an agent's action?
passages.text: Open the run on the Agents screen and read what it wants to do, field by field. Let it go ahead, or decline it. From a terminal, quilzo agent approve RUN STEP does the same.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Can a model change what an agent may do?
passages.text: No. Only a person can declare, change or withdraw an agent. A model chooses among the capabilities the declaration lists, and every action is checked against it.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › What if an agent reads a page with hidden instructions?
passages.text: It can still only do what it declared. Quilzo also notes that the run read stored content, and anything it produced then needs a person before it is relied on.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Budgets
passages.text: Steps, tool calls and minutes. A run that reaches one stops and says which.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Kept runs
passages.text: Every step and observation, readable later, and resumable if a run was cut off.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Probe
passages.text: Ask the gate whether an agent would be allowed to do something, without running it.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Any model
passages.text: Local through Ollama or llama.cpp, or hosted, through one gateway with budgets.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Agents as a log source
passages.text: What agents do flows into the security console, where new kinds of action are flagged.

passages.header: Agents that ask before they act › Agent cards
passages.text: Published as an A2A agent card, so other systems can find what an agent offers.

passages.header: Changelog
passages.text: **Chatbots on static sites.** A chatbot can now go with a site when it is exported to static files, and answer in the visitor's browser from the published pages, with no model. Its answers are tested against the server's. **Three new kinds of section.** Tabs, a row of quotes, and a question box that opens a chatbot with the question already asked. A hero can also show a large picture under its headline. **Quilzo watches itself.** Its own audit log and public site now feed the security console. Repeated failed sign-ins, new admin tokens, weakened settings, people probing for the admin and attempts to steer a chatbot all become findings. **Fourteen frameworks.** Posture checks are mapped to fourteen frameworks, including FedRAMP, the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001. When a check starts failing, a finding opens.

passages.header: Changelog
passages.text: **Talk to a person.** A chatbot can hand a conversation to a person. It arrives in the inbox, with a suggested reply. **Agents that wait.** Runs are kept as they go. An action marked ask-first waits for a person, and a run can be resumed or replayed from any step. **A new mark.** A Q in two parts: the loop in blue, and the tail in violet crossing its gap. What changed in Quilzo, written by the release-notes agent from the team's notes. What changed in October 2026 Written by Quilzo's release-notes agent from the team's raw notes, and published after a person approved it.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources
passages.text: A Quilzo chatbot answers from your published pages, links every answer to its source, says it is automated, and hands over to a person when it cannot help. Point it at your pages. It answers from them, quotes them, links to them, and says plainly when it does not know.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › Every answer links to where it came from
passages.text: A question answered with a quote and a link to its source page. A question is matched against your published pages two ways, and a page only counts if it covers most of what was asked. With no model, the answer is quoted from that page. With one, every sentence it writes is checked against the passages before you see it. Pages you exclude are never read, and drafts are never published to it.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › It says what it is
passages.text: Every conversation says it is automated, as the EU AI Act's Article 50 asks, and a compliance check flags a published page that leaves it out.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › It finds the pages
passages.text: Ranked two ways, by the words themselves and by overall similarity, and refused if no page covers the question.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › It answers, and cites
passages.text: Quoted, or written by a model and checked sentence by sentence against what it found.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › It hands over
passages.text: A visitor can ask for a person. The conversation lands in your inbox, kept only as long as you set.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › Try it
passages.text: This one answers in your browser, from this site, with no model.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › A person, when it matters
passages.text: The inbox: a visitor's conversation, handed over by the chatbot, with a reply being written. When a visitor asks for a person, the conversation arrives in the admin's inbox. Somebody answers there, with a suggested reply drafted from your pages if you want one, and the visitor sees it on the same page.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › Can the chatbot make things up?
passages.text: Without a model it cannot: it only quotes your pages. With a model, every sentence it writes is checked against the passages it found, and a sentence that fails the check is dropped before the visitor sees it.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › Can a visitor talk to a person?
passages.text: Yes, when the owner allows it. The visitor's conversation goes to the inbox, somebody answers it there, and the visitor sees the reply on the same page.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › Is anything a visitor asks stored?
passages.text: Questions to the chatbot are not stored. Only a conversation a visitor chooses to hand to a person is kept, for as long as the owner sets and at most ninety days, and the visitor is told so before they send it.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › Does it need a model?
passages.text: No. Without one it quotes your pages. With one, it writes an answer and every sentence is checked against the passages it found.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › Can it work on a static site?
passages.text: Yes. A chatbot marked for static copies goes with the site when it is exported, and answers in the visitor's browser. The one on this site does exactly that.

passages.header: Chatbots that show their sources › Can I put it on another site?
passages.text: Yes, in a frame, on the sites you list and nowhere else.

passages.header: Compliance it produces as it runs
passages.text: Quilzo maps its own checks to fourteen security, privacy and AI frameworks and runs them continuously against the live system. Checks that run against the live system, mapped to the frameworks your customers ask about.

passages.header: Compliance it produces as it runs › One check, every framework it satisfies
passages.text: Alt: The frameworks screen.. Each posture check is mapped to the controls it provides evidence for. When a check starts failing, the frameworks it affects show it, and a finding opens so somebody owns it.

passages.header: Compliance it produces as it runs › Mapped frameworks
passages.text: Fourteen frameworks: FedRAMP's three baselines share a row. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Security and privacy controls FedRAMP Low, Moderate and High US federal cloud security, on NIST SP 800-53 ISO/IEC 27001 Information security management SOC 2 Security, availability and confidentiality NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Cybersecurity outcomes HIPAA Security Rule US health information safeguards GDPR EU personal data protection CCPA and CPRA California consumer privacy EU AI Act Transparency and oversight of AI systems NIST AI RMF AI risk management ISO/IEC 42001 AI management systems OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications Risks specific to language models

passages.header: Compliance it produces as it runs › Evidence, not certification
passages.text: Quilzo produces evidence for these frameworks. Certification is still an auditor's decision about your organisation, and no software can make it for you.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act
passages.text: Quilzo is the open-source platform for AI agents, chatbots and the sites they live on. Every action is declared, every step is kept, and the ones that matter wait for a person. Build agents, chatbots and the sites they live on, in one open-source platform. Declare what an agent may do, watch every step it takes, and approve the ones that matter. Quilzo's admin showing an agent's run stopped before it writes a page: the exact call it wants to make, with buttons to let it go ahead or decline.

passages.text: The sections of this site's home page, in order, with buttons to move, edit or remove each one. Typed content, twenty-three kinds of section, and a theme whose every colour is contrast-checked. A page a reader could not use does not publish. Label: Sites.

passages.text: The findings queue: what the detections found, newest first, each with what it was about and what to do next. Collect sign-in and audit logs from Okta, Entra, GitHub and more, run tested detections over them, and work findings into cases. Quilzo reads its own audit log the same way. Label: Security.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Fourteen frameworks, checked as it runs
passages.text: The frameworks screen: each framework with how many of its mapped checks pass. FedRAMP, ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001 and more, mapped to checks that run against the live system. Evidence is something it produces, not something you collect. Label: Compliance.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › The model never holds the authority
passages.text: A kept agent run: each step it took, what it read, and the step where it stopped to ask. Most agent frameworks hand a model your tools and a system prompt asking it to behave. Then the model reads a page, an email or a ticket somebody else wrote, and does what it says. In Quilzo, every action passes one gate that checks it against the agent's declaration. A hijacked agent can still only do what it declared before anybody talked to it, and what you marked ask-first still waits for you.

passages.text: Passkeys, Google and Microsoft sign-in, scoped roles and tokens that expire.

passages.text: Every change, sign-in and agent action, chained so an edit to the past shows.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Publish anywhere
passages.text: Serve it yourself, or export static files for GitHub Pages, a bucket or IPFS. This site is one.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Analytics without cookies
passages.text: Visits, conversions and A/B tests, counted without identifying anybody.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Rules it keeps
passages.text: By: Agent Studio. Role: from Quilzo's design notes. A model can never declare, withdraw, approve or replay an agent. Those are a person's decisions. By: Ask-first runs. Role: from Quilzo's design notes. An approved action still passes the gate against the current declaration. Approval is not a way around it. By: Chatbots. Role: from Quilzo's design notes. Nothing a visitor asks a chatbot is stored. A conversation handed to a person is kept for a set number of days, and they are told so before they send it.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › What happens when an agent wants to publish?
passages.text: It stops and asks. A declaration can mark any capability ask-first, and when the agent reaches for it the run pauses: a person sees the exact page and fields it wants to write. Approving performs that stored call, still inside the declaration's limits. Declining refuses it, and the run carries on without it.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Which frameworks does Quilzo map?
passages.text: Fourteen: NIST SP 800-53, FedRAMP Low, Moderate and High, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the HIPAA Security Rule, GDPR, CCPA and CPRA, the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Does Quilzo need a database?
passages.text: No. Quilzo is one binary that keeps its content in a folder on disk, as files named by their contents, so there is no database to install, run or back up separately.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Can I use my own model?
passages.text: Yes. Quilzo talks to any model that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions protocol: a local one through Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or vLLM, or a hosted one with a key. The model gateway adds routes, fallbacks and budgets.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Is Quilzo free?
passages.text: Yes. It is open source under AGPL-3.0-or-later. A commercial licence is available for organisations that cannot use the AGPL, and it is the same program.

passages.header: AI agents that ask before they act › Run it on your laptop in a minute
passages.text: One binary, no database to install, and a local model if you want one.

passages.header: A security console that watches itself
passages.text: Collect logs from the tools you use, run tested detections, work findings into cases, and see Quilzo's own audit log the same way. Logs in, tested detections over them, findings worked into cases, and actions on other tools only when a second person approves.

passages.header: A security console that watches itself › What the detections found, and what to do next
passages.text: Alt: The findings queue.. Detections are Sigma-style rules, each with tests and a record of how often it was right. Findings group by person, so a pattern across several tools shows as one story. Quilzo's own audit log and public site are sources too: repeated failed sign-ins, admin tokens issued, settings weakened, people probing for the admin, and visitors trying to steer the chatbot all become findings.
